title: OpenWorker
description: Metrics of the OpenWorker servers: the world loop, handlers, simulation, sessions, Redis, Postgres and the .NET runtime. Provisioned from eng/observability.

panels.title: Sessions active
panels.description: Open connections, all the processes shown.

panels.title: Loop queue, worst
panels.description: The longest queue of callbacks waiting for the world loop.

panels.title: Loop callback p99
panels.description: How long the slowest 1% of callbacks hold the world loop.

panels.title: Simulation step p99
panels.description: One tick of the clock against its budget of 50 ms.

panels.title: Handler errors / min
panels.description: Packets that failed to parse or to handle.

panels.title: Sessions closed / min
panels.description: All the reasons together.

panels.title: Loop queue length
panels.description: Callbacks posted to the world loop that have not started. A queue that does not drain is a loop that is behind.

panels.title: Loop callback duration (p50, p99)
panels.description: How long one callback holds the thread of the loop: a handler, the continuation after an await, a timer. Everything else on the process waits for it.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, job, instance, openworker_location) (rate(worldloop_callback_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, job, instance, openworker_location) (rate(worldloop_callback_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Handler duration p99 by opcode (top 10)
panels.description: From the start of the handler to the end of its task, so the waits for Redis and the database are in it. The packets nobody handles share the tag `unhandled`.

panels.title: Handler calls per second by opcode (top 10)
Handler errors by reason, refused packets by group
panels.description: `malformed`: the packet is not what the client should send. `handler_fault`: the handler failed on a packet that parsed. `violation`: the handler refused what the packet asks as impossible (a move faster than the hero runs). `refused`: packets dropped because the session sent their group faster than `Hotspot:RateLimits` allows.

panels.title: Handler duration p50 overall
panels.description: All opcodes together.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, job, instance, openworker_location) (rate(handler_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Simulation step duration (p50, p99)
panels.description: One tick of the clock, all the mazes together. The line is the budget of 50 ms.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, job, instance, openworker_location) (rate(simulation_step_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, job, instance, openworker_location) (rate(simulation_step_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Steps over budget per minute
panels.description: Ticks that took longer than 50 ms.

panels.title: Sessions active
panels.description: Open connections per process.

panels.title: Sessions closed per minute by reason
panels.description: `client`: the client left or the socket failed. `server`: closed by the server with no reason of its own to name. `backpressure`: the client does not read what it is sent. `timeout`: no answer to keep-alives. `malformed`: too many bad packets.

panels.title: Writer queue length
panels.description: Frames queued to be sent, over all the connections of the process. One connection holds at most 4096.

panels.title: Frames sent per second
panels.description: Frames written to sockets, and the messages dropped because they do not fit one frame, by opcode.

panels.title: Bytes sent per second
panels.description: Headers included.

panels.title: Bytes received per second
panels.description: Headers included.

panels.title: Redis call duration p99 by operation
panels.description: The name of the Redis command, as the connection measured it from the moment it was made to its answer.

panels.title: Redis calls per second by operation
Postgres call duration p99 by operation
panels.description: The kind of the SQL statement. The time until the database starts to answer.

panels.title: Postgres calls per second by operation
GC pause time per second
panels.description: Seconds the process spent paused by the GC in each second.

panels.title: GC collections per second by generation
GC heap after the last collection by generation
Allocation rate
panels.description: Bytes allocated on the managed heap per second.

panels.title: CPU time per second
panels.description: Cores in use.

panels.title: Thread pool queue length
panels.description: Work items waiting for a thread of the pool.

panels.title: Thread pool work items per second
